# Closing its own loops: what an AI system that runs itself shows about the human in every step

> Ultrastable is the foundation for any autonomous system.

## Abstract

Ultrastable R&D (Ultrastable): A common belief holds that AI agents can draft code but a person must still merge it, deploy it and check that it works. Ultrastable is built to close those loops itself: a server-side lane merges green changes, every deploy is proven live against its commit, and every loop names its closing probe. We state the common belief as properties that can fail, and test each against the records of a system that merges, deploys and checks its own work. Where it still depends on outside sessions, the paper says so with the number. 4 of 6 are met today; each one that is not is an open work item with a closing probe, and this paper is regenerated from the measurements after every merge.

## The study

Can an AI system close its own loops?. Ultrastable R&D, Ultrastable; own R&D question set, regenerated from this system's records, version 2026-11-21. Data: This system's own ledgers: closed pull requests read from GitHub, the deploy record, the criticality ticks, the ultrastability ledger and the loop registry.

## Findings, mechanisms and measurements

### O1. Every loop says how it closes (systems)

**The study:** Belief: an automated process needs a person to notice when it is done. Test: every registered loop declares a closing probe and a server-side owner. (Loop registry)

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- SERVER-OWNS-LOOPS-1 (`foundation/loopowner.py`): a loop with no server-side owner fails the build
- CLOCKWORK-1 (`instances/ultrastable/loop-registry.json`): each loop row carries its trigger, closing probe and owner

**Measured here:** share of registered loops that declare a closing probe and a server-side owner: 1.0 (n = 112). Target >= 1.0. Verdict: **met**.
Source: instances/ultrastable/loop-registry.json (declared).

### O2. Merging needs no person (oversight)

**The study:** Belief: a change waits for a person to merge it. Test: median hours from a pull request opening to its merge. (Merge lane)

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- AUTO-SHIP-CLEAN-1 (`seed/worker/src/sweeper.js`): the server-side sweeper merges a green pull request
- DRAIN-ALL-1 (`seed/worker/src/lane.js`): the lane reconciles conflicts with main and retries

**Measured here:** median hours from a pull request opening to its merge: 0.15 (n = 64). Target <= 1.0. Verdict: **met**.
Source: GitHub REST pulls?state=closed, last 100 closed pull requests, fetched 2026-11-21T09:30:00Z.

### O3. Deploys are checked by the system (reliability)

**The study:** Belief: someone has to check that a deploy really worked. Test: share of uploaded deploys proven live against their own commit. (Deploy record)

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- HANDOFF-1 (`deploy/deploy-workers.mjs`): every deploy is read back and compared with its commit before it counts

**Measured here:** share of uploaded deploys proven live against their commit: 1.0 (n = 40). Target >= 0.95. Verdict: **met**.
Source: ops/deploys.jsonl (same window).

### O4. No person in the path (oversight)

**The study:** Belief: automation still needs a hand on the wheel. Test: human touches counted by the latest criticality tick. (Criticality ledger)

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- CRITICALITY-1 (`foundation/criticality.py`): human touches are counted in the denominator of the system's own score

**Measured here:** human touches counted by the latest criticality tick: 0 (n = 0). Target <= 0. Verdict: **met**.
Source: ops/criticality.jsonl at 2026-11-24T17:40:23Z.

### O5. The system starts its own work (systems)

**The study:** Belief: an AI system only does what a person asks. Test: share of merged pull requests the system's own loops opened. (Pull request record)

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- SELF-REFERENCE-1 (`foundation/executor.py`): the executor takes items from the queue in driver order and opens its own pull requests

Source: GitHub REST pulls?state=closed, last 100 closed pull requests, fetched 2026-11-21T09:30:00Z.

**The study:** Belief: shipping to production needs a person. Test: verified deploys the system originated and executed itself. (Criticality ledger)

## Limits

- Scale. One organization: 100 closed pull requests (64 merged) over 0.75 days. Our numbers describe this system; they are not a causal estimate and are not compared with the study's effect sizes as if they were.
- Who wrote the changes. 80% of merged pull requests in the window were opened by code agent sessions run under the owner's account, not by the system's own loops. The latest criticality tick puts the system in the subcritical regime with 0 self-originated deploys, so most of the work measured here was started from outside.
- Review by construction. Ultrastable has no human review step, so a short open-to-merge time is partly a consequence of the design. The real test of the design is quality: the revert and deploy-verification findings, which can fail.
- Revert share counts commits whose subject starts with Revert; a fix that undoes a change without that word is not counted, so the figure is a lower bound.
- Source. Own r&d question set, regenerated from this system's records, version 2026-11-21; its findings may change in later versions.
